scenes.line1: How do you group and filter data?
scenes.say: When should you use WHERE, and when should you use HAVING to filter results in SQL?

scenes.label: GROUP BY
scenes.sub: Groups rows by column values for aggregation
scenes.say: Group By lets you organize rows into groups based on column values. This is the first step to summarizing data.

scenes.code:
SELECT department_id,
       COUNT(*)
FROM employees
GROUP BY department_id;
scenes.say: Here, we count how many employees are in each department. Count is just one of several aggregate functions you can use.
Where filters rows before grouping. Having filters groups after you've calculated aggregates. Use Having when your condition depends on the result of an aggregate function.

scenes.question: Where do you filter by COUNT(*)?
scenes.right: Use HAVING COUNT(*) > 10 to filter groups after aggregation.
scenes.say: Don't trip up: you can't use Where to filter by count. You need Having for that.
